clue.text: Work unit accepting a learner in eastern city

indicators.note: accepting means the work unit takes the following letters inside itself

parts.note: a man-day is a unit of work, one person's labour for one day
L is the learner driver's plate letter

explanation.surface: A labour measure that takes on a trainee somewhere in an eastern city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' puts A and L inside MANDAY, after its first four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandalay is a major city of Myanmar, in the East.

clue.text: Measurement taken from lighthouse

indicators.note: taken from signals letters lifted straight out of the word lighthouse

explanation.surface: Someone takes a reading from a lighthouse.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits in the middle of 'lighthouse'.
explanation.definitionFit: A thou is a thousandth of an inch, a small engineering measurement.

clue.text: Relative study which incorporates American one

indicators.note: which incorporates says the study word holds the following pieces inside it

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A family-member study that includes an American subject.
explanation.definitionFit: A cousin is a family member, the child of an aunt or uncle.

clue.text: Nervous in the extreme?

parts.note: read 'in the extreme' as being at the very border or rim of something, while the whole also means highly tense

explanation.surface: Someone very tense.
explanation.walkthrough: Something placed at the extreme is right at its edge, so the word for jittery also describes being at the brink.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgy means tense and on edge, so very nervous.

clue.text: Taurus and Leo as used by native Australians in religious rites?

definitions.text: as used by native Australians in religious rites?

parts.note: Taurus is the zodiac sign of the bull
Leo is the lion, an animal that roars

explanation.surface: Two star signs turned to sacred use by Aboriginal Australians.
explanation.walkthrough: The two zodiac animals are clued by what they are and what they do: the lion is a roarer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bullroarer is a slat of wood whirled on a cord to make a roaring hum in Aboriginal ceremonies.

clue.text: I abandoned liaison upsetting woman

indicators.note: upsetting means the remaining letters are knocked into a new order
abandoned means the letter I is dropped from the following word

explanation.surface: Someone walks out of a love affair, distressing a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' takes I out of LIAISON, leaving LIASON, which 'upsetting' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Alison is a woman's given name.

clue.text: Austrian physicist is second to identify male quality

parts.note: Ernst Mach was an Austrian physicist, of Mach numbers
a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: A famous Austrian scientist is quick to pin down a masculine trait.
explanation.walkthrough: MO, as in 'half a mo', means a brief moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Machismo is aggressive, swaggering manliness.

clue.text: Parts of vessels coming over to headland having clean lines?

indicators.note: coming over in a down clue means the word for ship parts is flipped upwards

parts.note: keels are the bottom timbers of ships
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness

explanation.surface: Ships' parts are carried over to a promontory, looking streamlined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming over' turns KEELS to read SLEEK.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleekness is smooth, streamlined elegance of shape.

clue.text: Blue drunk after party-that's the spirit

indicators.note: after places the scrambled colour word behind the party word

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters stagger into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A depressed tipsy guest after a party toasts the right attitude.
explanation.definitionFit: A double is a ghostly counterpart or wraith, a kind of spirit.

clue.text: Day by river? Plunge into water

parts.note: the Ouse is an English river, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A day beside a river, ready for a swim.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is the name of several rivers in England.
explanation.definitionFit: To douse is to drench or plunge into liquid.

clue.text: What would help you see agent with drink?

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
a glass is a drink, as in 'a glass of wine'

explanation.surface: A drink might help a secret agent see better.
explanation.definitionFit: A spyglass is a small telescope for viewing distant things.

clue.text: Shocking lab crackdown on pioneer aviators

indicators.note: shocking suggests the letters are jolted into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A scandalous clampdown in a laboratory affecting early flyers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shocking' rearranges LAB CRACKDOWN ON; 'on' is part of the fodder, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: John Alcock and Arthur Brown made the first non-stop transatlantic flight in 1919.

clue.text: Jogging along to aid toothache

indicators.note: jogging means jolting the letters loose into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Running about as a cure for a sore tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: Odontalgia is the medical term for pain in a tooth.

clue.text: Appropriate to ask about it appearing in paper — pink, in the middle

indicators.note: about means the asking word wraps around everything that follows

parts.note: to beg is to ask

indicators.note: appearing in puts the word it inside the newspaper abbreviation

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper
taken as written

indicators.note: in the middle takes the central letters of the word pink

explanation.surface: Fitting to request something shown in a pink newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: IT goes inside FT to make FITT; add IN, the middle of 'pink', and 'about' puts FITTIN inside BEG. The FT is printed on pink paper, which makes the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Befitting means suitable or proper for the occasion.

clue.text: Potential enemy receives officials

annotationWithheld.why: 'Potential enemy receives officials': ENEMY rearranged gives five of YEOMEN's six letters, but no clue word supplies the O ('receives' is only the container); a word such as 'nothing' or 'love' seems lost in OCR and no print found.

clue.text: A force to become irritated in fight

parts.note: F is the physics symbol for force
to fray is to become strained or irritated, as tempers fray

explanation.surface: Pressure makes someone lose their temper in a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: Affray is a legal term in Britain for a public fight that frightens others.
explanation.definitionFit: An affray is a brawl or disturbance of the peace.

clue.text: US university head typically having this security device?

parts.note: Yale is a university in Connecticut
a head usually has a lock, a tress of hair

explanation.surface: An American college principal keeps a door fastening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' looks like the head of a university, but it is a person's head, which bears locks of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yale lock is a cylinder lock with a pin-tumbler key, common on front doors.

clue.text: Disconcerted if Royalist acts in an acceptable way

indicators.note: disconcerted means thrown into confusion, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A flustered monarchist behaves well enough.
explanation.definitionFit: Satisfactorily means adequately, in a way that meets requirements.

clue.text: Not well expressed in English — surreptitious all round

annotationWithheld.clue: Not well expressed in English — surreptitious all round

clue.text: One on the conservative side, properly

parts.note: A means one, as in 'a dog'
the political right is the conservative side

explanation.surface: Someone leaning to the right behaves properly.
explanation.definitionFit: Aright means correctly or in the proper way.

clue.text: A good story-teller in Channel Islands capital

indicators.note: in places the run of pieces inside the Channel Islands letters

parts.note: a liar tells stories, untrue ones

explanation.surface: A fine raconteur turns up in the islands' main town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'story-teller' looks complimentary but means someone telling fibs; CI is the Channel Islands, the British islands off Normandy.
explanation.definitionFit: Cagliari is the capital city of Sardinia.

clue.text: Top expert pockets money

indicators.note: pockets means the expert word holds the money letter inside

parts.note: an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A skilled player keeps the winnings.
explanation.definitionFit: The acme is the peak or highest point.

clue.text: Force politician into convoluted lie

indicators.note: into means the politician goes inside the twisted word
convoluted means twisted, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Pressure a politician into telling a tangled untruth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'convoluted' turns LIE into IEL, and MP goes in after the I.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to drive or push someone to act.

clue.text: President consumed starter

parts.note: ate means consumed

explanation.surface: The head of state ate the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: PATE is entered without its accent; 'consumed' looks like part of the dinner scene but supplies ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Pâté is a meat or fish paste served as a first course.

clue.text: Images misrepresented

annotationWithheld.why: 'Images misrepresented': rearranging IMAGES gives the letters, but no clue word defines prejudice against the old; the clue appears cut short in OCR and no print found.

clue.text: Superior kind of college depending a lot on electronics

parts.note: high means superior, upper
a tech is a technical college

explanation.surface: An upper-class college relies heavily on gadgets.
explanation.walkthrough: A tech is British shorthand for a technical college.
explanation.definitionFit: High-tech describes advanced technology, heavily electronic.
